description: Named exception-handler matching: EXCEPTION WHEN <user_exception_name> must catch a RAISE of that SAME declared exception, and only that one. The exception MESSAGES here deliberately do NOT contain the exception name, so a catch proves real NAME-matching rather than a coincidental message substring, which was the previous behaviour. A non-matching named handler does not catch, so the raised exception propagates with its own message and the handler body never runs. A matching named handler wins over a WHEN OTHER written beside it. And WHEN OTHER on its own remains a catch-all for a RAISEd user exception, which is the regression guard. Converted 1:1 from scripting/NamedExceptionHandlerTest (now retired).

steps.sql: DECLARE my_exc EXCEPTION (-20002, 'boom'); BEGIN RAISE my_exc; EXCEPTION WHEN my_exc THEN INSERT INTO caught VALUES (1); END;
DECLARE err_a EXCEPTION (-20001, 'aaa'); err_b EXCEPTION (-20002, 'bbb'); BEGIN RAISE err_a; EXCEPTION WHEN err_b THEN INSERT INTO caught VALUES (1); END;
DECLARE my_exc EXCEPTION (-20002, 'boom'); BEGIN RAISE my_exc; EXCEPTION WHEN my_exc THEN INSERT INTO caught VALUES (1); WHEN OTHER THEN INSERT INTO caught VALUES (2); END;
DECLARE my_exc EXCEPTION (-20002, 'boom'); BEGIN RAISE my_exc; EXCEPTION WHEN OTHER THEN INSERT INTO caught VALUES (7); END;
